avertissement: Traductions automatiques des textes français ; chaque nombre a été vérifié contre le français. Les documents de la Ville sont en français et font foi.

canopee.description: Tree planting, greening, and the fight against emerald ash borer and heat islands.
canopee.enBref: The City buys trees and pays for their planting on sidewalks, in parks and on private land. It also funds the machinery and employee teams that do this work in the boroughs. At the same time, borough councils allow construction projects to depart from the rules on trees and greening.

etapes.titre: Contracts for tree planting on public land
etapes.texte: City council awards two contracts to supply and plant 1,374 trees in seven boroughs, then water them, maintain them and replace some of them. The maximum expenditure is $2,456,590.55, taxes included.

The City pays $3,071,550 to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain to plant and maintain trees on private and institutional land until December 31, 2026. Pierrefonds-Roxboro, for its part, transfers $162,233.12 from the parks fund to buy trees and plants.

etapes.titre: Exceptions to the rules on trees
etapes.texte: Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve authorizes an expansion on rue Préfontaine with 25 trees and 5% greening instead of the required 40 trees and 25%. Montréal-Nord allows trees to be planted less than 1.5 metres from the street line at 5745, boulevard Léger.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve rents a mini-backhoe loader with operator for $152,916.75 and sets aside $200,000 for blue-collar teams assigned to planting. Outremont awards the renovation of the parc Pratt chalet and the redevelopment of its surroundings, including planting vegetation, for an expenditure of $800,416.17, partly funded by the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux.

The City leases parcels in the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain for $100, so that it can operate a transitional nursery there. The lease runs for 24 months starting May 1, 2026, and the property subsidy is estimated at $329,600.

aSurveiller.texte: The Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain must submit a progress report on October 31, 2026, its accountability report by December 31, 2026 at the latest, then its summary and financial statements on March 31, 2027.
The 855 trees in lot 2 must be planted in spring 2027; watering, maintenance and replacement continue until the end of November 2029.
The lease for the transitional nursery ends on April 30, 2028.

deneigement.description: Contracts for snow removal and snow loading, spreading of abrasives, parking by-laws.

etapes.titre: Spring cleaning of streets and sidewalks
etapes.texte: Several boroughs are renting vacuum sweepers, tanker trucks, sidewalk washers and a mini sweeper with operators to remove abrasives after winter. Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is also awarding the cleaning of sidewalks in four private snow removal sectors, for $271,979.11 including taxes.

etapes.titre: Snow removal at downtown public squares
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie is awarding the maintenance, cleanliness and snow removal of Square Viger and Place des Montréalaises, then of six squares including square Dorchester and square Victoria. The borough is also extending snow removal for the Quartier des Spectacles by one year, from April 2, 2026 to April 1, 2027.

The City is retaining towing companies for Montréal-Nord and Le Plateau-Mont-Royal, and six snow transport contracts covering five boroughs. It is also extending snow removal for parc Frédéric-Back, the TAZ and the soccer stadium, and awarding snow removal for the Grand parc de l'Ouest; Ville-Marie is extending maintenance of the esplanade Tranquille.

aSurveiller.texte: Towing related to snow removal in Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is scheduled from November 15, 2026 to March 31, 2027.
Snow removal for the Grand parc de l'Ouest (Anse-à-l'Orme, Bois-de-la-Roche, Cap-Saint-Jacques) covers two seasons, from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
The turnkey snow removal contract for Le Plateau-Mont-Royal ends on April 15, 2031; those for Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Lachine, Outremont and Le Sud-Ouest end on April 15, 2030.

eau-egouts.description: Pipes, drinking water production plants, the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, retention basins.
eau-egouts.enBref: The City is funding and carrying out work on its water networks and on the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant. It is awarding contracts to rehabilitate water pipes, rebuild sewer and water pipes under several streets, and replace lead service lines. It is also passing loan by-laws for the wastewater disinfection plant and for network renewal.

etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council is increasing from $197,000,000 to $381,000,000 the loan that funds the disinfection unit at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant. The money is to be used to finish building the ozonation unit, install liquid oxygen tanks and build the oxygen production plant.

The City is awarding a series of contracts to rehabilitate secondary water pipes by lining, without digging trenches, and to redo the road surface on streets in several boroughs. These contracts include replacing lead water service connections, on both the public side and the private side.

The City is awarding contracts to rebuild or rehabilitate water and sewer pipes, with road resurfacing, notably on rue Guy, rue De Champlain and rue de la Cathédrale. On rue de la Cathédrale, it is adding $12,144,522.14 in contingencies after a new inspection of the pipe.

aSurveiller.texte: Adoption expected on November 16, 2026 of the by-law amending the by-law on connections to the waterworks and sewer networks and on stormwater management (20-030).
Commissioning of the ozone plant at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant expected in 2029; the contracts for lots 4, 5 and 6 are to be completed in the last quarter of 2028.
End of work on the rue de la Cathédrale pipe pushed back from December 2026 to March 2027.
Rue Guy worksite expected to run until December 2027.
Federal grant of up to $128.3M conditional on the infrastructure being completed by 2031 for the Namur-De la Savane sector.

frederic-back.titre: Frédéric-Back Park and Saint-Michel Environmental Complex
frederic-back.description: The former quarry turned dump, transformed into a park in phases: urban greenhouses, biogas capture, electrical system rationalization.
frederic-back.enBref: This year, the City is continuing work on Frédéric-Back park, on the site of the Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel. It is launching the construction of a greenhouse complex in the Saint-Michel neighbourhood, awarding contracts for park maintenance and electrical work related to biogas capture, and funding the redevelopment of rue De Louvain along the edge of the park. It is also filing applications for financial assistance with the Quebec and Canada governments.

etapes.titre: Funding request for the footbridge and east-west link
etapes.texte: The City is asking Quebec's ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable for assistance of up to $2,000,000 for a 900-metre multi-use path crossing the park from east to west, with a footbridge of about 150 metres. The project includes stormwater management works and a 12.7-hectare meadow.

etapes.titre: Green light for the greenhouse project
etapes.texte: The agglomeration approves the construction of a greenhouse complex near the composting platform: 1,500 m² for research and training, 1,000 m² for the community greenhouse, with a construction budget estimated at $2,185,000. The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension offers to carry out the project and city council accepts.

The City awards Groupe Nicky the park's general maintenance ($1,089,868.72) and Entreprises Roseneige the ecological and horticultural management ($838,793.21), from May 1, 2026 to October 31, 2028. It awards Systèmes Urbains inc. the second phase of the electrical system rationalization at the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel, which includes a new 25 kV power supply, a backup generator and a controller to manage biogas capture.

etapes.titre: Rue De Louvain and greenhouse assembly
etapes.texte: The borough awards Groupe MPotvin the redevelopment of rue De Louvain, between the park and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum of $8,199,514.82, taxes included: sewers, waterworks, lighting, cycling facilities, plantings. It then awards Les industries Harnois inc. the supply and installation of the greenhouse complex, for a maximum of $499,865.92, taxes included.

The City extends by five months the rental of a compost screener and a loader tractor with operator from Matériaux Paysagers Savaria ltée; this compost is used in particular for the park's development. It also extends by six months the snow removal contract for the park, the TAZ and the soccer stadium awarded to Groupe Nicky.

aSurveiller.texte: The call for projects under the TAPU program of the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable ends on November 26, 2026.
Installation work on the greenhouse complex must be completed by December 2026, and it is set to come into service in winter 2027.
Snow removal for the park, the TAZ and the soccer stadium is extended from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027.
Work on rue De Louvain continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks, curbs, bump-outs), then from May to August 2028 (final roadway, bike path, plantings).
The contracts for the park's general maintenance and ecological and horticultural management run until October 31, 2028; 26 hectares will be added to the park in 2027 in the Boisé Ouest sector.

grand-parc-ouest.description: The largest municipal park in Canada, being assembled: land acquisitions, Anse-à-l'Orme, Cap-Saint-Jacques, Bois-de-la-Roche, parc-nature des Sources.
grand-parc-ouest.enBref: This year, the City is maintaining and protecting the sectors of the Grand parc de l'Ouest. It adjusted a contract for the repair of heritage walls on chemin de Senneville, submitted a candidacy for an international designation related to the night sky at Cap-Saint-Jacques, and had two sectors listed in a registry of protected natural environments. It also awarded contracts for culvert reconstruction, snow removal, tree felling and housekeeping.

etapes.titre: More money for the heritage walls
etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98, taxes included, to the contract for the repair of the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville, bringing the contract to $1,174,331.77. Buried stones, extra mortar and a deteriorated culvert explain the increase, according to file 1255414002.

The City submits the candidacy of the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector (330 hectares) for the Urban Night Sky Place designation from DarkSky International. It commits to producing a lighting plan, bringing its light fixtures up to standard, and keeping nighttime access open to the public.

etapes.titre: Two sectors listed as natural environments
etapes.texte: The parc-nature des Sources (38.32 ha) and the Anse-à-l'Orme sector (429 ha) are listed in the Répertoire des milieux naturels protégés et contributifs à la biodiversité, with conservation plans. Elected officials also review the 2025 summary of the areas.

The City awards contracts for snow removal on the service roads and parking lots of Anse-à-l'Orme, Bois-de-la-Roche and Cap-Saint-Jacques, as well as housekeeping of nine buildings at Cap-Saint-Jacques, including the chalet d'accueil, Maison Richer and Château Gohier.

aSurveiller.texte: Snow removal of roads and parking lots from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028, with no possible extension.
Housekeeping of the nine Cap-Saint-Jacques buildings from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2030, with a possible extension to October 31, 2031.
Tree felling planned from fall 2026 to early summer 2028.
For the night sky designation: lighting plan submitted in February 2027, response from DarkSky expected in April 2027, site compliance by April 2032.

itinerance.description: Support for organizations, warming centres and shelters for people experiencing homelessness.
itinerance.enBref: The City lends municipal buildings to organizations so they can open warming centres, and gives money to organizations that work with people experiencing homelessness. It also shares, between boroughs, a public works team assigned to cleanliness related to homelessness. It has set up a framework for receiving private donations and has entrusted organizations with guiding people toward shelter and housing.

etapes.texte: The City lends three buildings free of charge to organizations to host people experiencing homelessness: the church at 5600, 12e Avenue in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, the former monastery at 12050, boulevard Gouin Est, and the Bain St-Denis, at 7075, rue Saint-Hubert. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie transfers $250,000 for the fit-up work of the Bain Saint-Denis warming centre, and Ahuntsic-Cartierville raises to $126,615.07, taxes included, the operating contract for a warming centre for winter 2025-2026.

Verdun pays $12,950 to the Société de développement social to keep two outreach workers in its municipal facilities from January 5 to February 6, 2026. The City then grants support of $5,407,736 to fifteen organizations and additional support of $3,942,461 to ten already-funded organizations, under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs.

City council adopts a declaration in support of people experiencing homelessness and in recognition of the organization Maison Mobile. The City then adopts a mechanism to receive private money donations intended for housing, shelter and social cohabitation: donors do not choose the project funded and the City may refuse a donation.

The City adds $860,692 to the shuttle agreements with Projets Autochtones du Québec, Mission Old Brewery and L'Amour en action Syl Dan, and extends these agreements. It also grants seven service contracts, for $3,025,000 taxes included, to implement the Programme d'interventions spécialisées en campement.

aSurveiller.texte: The ruling on the merits of the dispute over the encampments under the viaduc Van Horne is expected likely in 2027.
The shuttle agreements with three organizations are extended until December 31, 2027.
The public works team works in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles from May 15, 2026 to May 15, 2027.
The support under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs covers a three-year period ending December 31, 2028.

logement.description: Grants, land and social, affordable or student housing projects, including those of the SHDM and the OMHM.

etapes.texte: City council approves the SHDM's 2026 budget and the OMHM's budget, and the urban agglomeration council also approves the OMHM's 2026 budget. According to the file, the OMHM's total budget goes from $541M in 2025 to $605.6M in 2026.

The City accepts from the Government of Canada half of the rights to a 3,658.8 square metre site on rue Jolicoeur, in Pierrefonds-Roxboro, at no cost. It also transfers, at no cost, to the Coopérative d'habitation Monde-Uni a 789.6 square metre site at 7965, boulevard de l'Acadie, and authorizes a devaluation of $110,000.

The City adds $877,312 to its assistance to Mission Unitaînés and grants $581,845 to the Coopérative d'habitation Monde-Uni for the Acadie project. It buys a 1,535.1 square metre site in the Sud-Ouest for $9,293,113 for social housing purposes, and removes eleven lots from the list of properties subject to the right of first refusal.

The City pays $25,110,800 to the Société du Patrimoine Angus Résidentiel to build 350 affordable housing units in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie. The executive committee authorizes the SHDM to build a 72-unit building on the "Solotech" site, on 2e Avenue.

The City grants $13,151,528 to Immobilier collectif – Point commun for 395 housing units in the Sud-Ouest, $8,600,000 to Mission Unitaînés for housing for seniors in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles, $500,000 to the Société de développement Écoquartier Louvain and an additional $475,000 to Mission Old Brewery. It buys a site on rue de la Montagne for $500,000 and a 1,850 square metre site in Ville-Marie for $3,233,628, which it transfers at no cost to the SHDM.

aSurveiller.texte: Ville-Marie must adopt, on November 10, 2026, its by-law reducing public domain occupancy fees for construction sites that include social, affordable or non-market housing units.
Occupancy expected by April 30, 2027 at the latest for the 350 affordable housing units at Technopôle Angus.
Delivery expected in May 2028 for the SHDM's 72-unit building on 2e Avenue.
Occupancy expected in February 2030 for the 395-unit building in Pointe-Saint-Charles.

louvain-est.description: The neighbourhood being built on municipal land in Ahuntsic-Cartierville: acquisitions, soil decontamination, street names, temporary developments.

etapes.titre: Land leased and loaned on the site
etapes.texte: The City is leasing parts of the land south of rue de Louvain Ouest to the Société de transport de Montréal and to a parking company, and is loaning them free of charge to organizations for a vegetable garden, a greenhouse and sunflowers. It is also asking city council to entrust it with the lease of a 78,244-square-foot lot loaned to Îlot 84 for programming activities, and is paying $35,000 to this organization for the Esplanade - Louvain temporary space, from June 9 to December 31, 2026.

etapes.titre: Redevelopment of rue de Louvain Est
etapes.texte: The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is entrusting Groupe MPotvin with the redevelopment of rue de Louvain between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, at a maximum price of $8,199,514.82 taxes included, with sewer, water main, roadway, lighting and planting work. It will then request financial assistance from the ministère des Transports for the bike lane and sidewalks. Ahuntsic-Cartierville is changing the direction of lanes at the intersection of rue de Louvain Est and avenue Christophe-Colomb.
City council is naming the new street at the heart of the écoquartier "avenue des Solidarités." The name comes from a public call for proposals held in fall 2024.

The City is awarding Charex inc. a contract worth $10,311,940.25 taxes included to build 610 metres of street with sewer, water main, lighting and electrical network, and to clean up the soil of the former gas station on the Louvain Est lot. The total authorized expenditure reaches $15,366,336 taxes included.

The borough is authorizing an event-based and temporary use on the vacant lot at 50 and 150, rue de Louvain Ouest. It is also advancing a draft by-law that raises the height limit to 73 metres on part of this lot, and a special project allowing the demolition of a building on avenue de l'Esplanade and the construction of a group of buildings.

The City is adding $48,398.55 to Loiselle inc.'s contract for sewer, water main and site preparation work related to the modular housing on the Louvain Ouest site, bringing this contract to $914,546.41 taxes included. It is also granting $500,000 to the Société de développement Écoquartier Louvain for the design of an off-market housing project.

aSurveiller.texte: Work on rue de Louvain continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks, curbs, bump-outs), then from May to August 2028 (final roadway surface, bike path, planting).
The parking lease with the Société de transport de Montréal begins October 1, 2026 and lasts three years, at a rate of 92 days per year.
The loan of the land for the sunflowers and the greenhouse runs from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2027; the one for the vegetable garden ends December 31, 2027.
Four other public places on the site remain to be named before development is completed, expected around 2032.

matieres-residuelles.description: Collection, sorting centres, biomethanation and ecocentres.
matieres-residuelles.enBref: This year, the City is adjusting its collection rules in several boroughs, buying bins and extending contracts for food waste treatment and transport for ecocentres. It is also awarding hydro-excavation contracts with residual materials treatment in several boroughs. The 2025 residual materials management report and the Inspector General's reports on subcontracting collections are being tabled at councils.

etapes.texte: The executive committee is changing collection days, schedules and sectors in L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève, Le Plateau-Mont-Royal and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, where garbage is collected every two weeks from November 1 to April 30 and every week from May 1 to October 31. Two boroughs are also authorizing waste-related arrangements in buildings: a storage room of at least 28 m² at 397, boulevard Saint-Joseph Ouest, and an exemption from an outdoor storage area at 2380, rue Notre-Dame Ouest.

The City is extending its contracts with Recyclage Notre-Dame inc. twice, by six months each time, to compost or biomethanize food waste from the eastern part of the agglomeration, at $3,269,055.43 taxes included per extension. It explains that the start-up of the Montréal-Est organic materials treatment centre is not confirmed and that it can end the contracts with 30 days' notice.

The City is entering into framework agreements to supply collection bins, including one with Plasti-Bac inc. for garbage bins intended for Ahuntsic-Cartierville and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, where garbage collection will be spaced out. Ahuntsic-Cartierville is giving Ville en vert a mandate for information and awareness-raising, and the executive committee is approving an agreement with Tricentris to lend reusable dishware, water fountains and sorting stations for neighbourhood events.

The City is extending the contract for supplying and transporting containers for the écocentre Saint-Laurent, as well as the contracts for collecting garbage from front-loading and semi-underground containers. It is awarding Recyc-Matelas inc. a contract worth $734,690.25 taxes included, over 28 months, to collect and recover mattresses and box springs left at ecocentres.

aSurveiller.texte: The extension of the food waste treatment contracts runs until February 28, 2027.
The écocentre Saint-Laurent container contract and the collection contracts by containers are extended until October 31, 2027.
The discharge authorization management software contract covers the period from October 12, 2026 to October 11, 2029.

namur-hippodrome.description: The new neighbourhood on the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack: sale of land, loan by-laws, water mains in the Namur–De la Savane sector.
namur-hippodrome.enBref: On the site of the former racetrack, the City is preparing the land and financing for the future neighbourhood. It obtained more time from the Québec government to sell a first parcel of land, adopted loan by-laws for the water mains and streets, and transferred a parcel of land to an organization for non-market housing. At the same time, it is leasing parcels of land that are still vacant to urban agriculture and greening organizations.

etapes.titre: Deadline to sell a parcel of land postponed
etapes.texte: The Québec government grants the City a deadline of October 31, 2027 to sell a first parcel of land on the site, west of boulevard Décarie and south of rue Paré. The postponement does not entail any financial compensation and the other conditions of the 2017 deed of transfer remain the same.

The City guarantees a $2,000,000 loan from the Canada Infrastructure Bank to Société GALOPH, a non-profit organization, to pay for feasibility studies for the residential project. On the same day, city council rejects a motion from the Official Opposition on the governance and management of the neighbourhood's assets and public funds.

The City adopts a $29,000,000 loan to develop the neighbourhood's public domain: soil remediation, sewers and water mains, street redevelopment and land purchases. It also adopts a $12,000,000 loan to build main water mains between boulevard Cavendish, in Saint-Laurent, and rue Isabella, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.

The City leases parcels of land on the site to MultiCaf and to the Coopérative de solidarité Polliflora for temporary urban agriculture, and to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain for a transition nursery. Each lease provides for a nominal rent, with the organizations paying for development, upkeep and property taxes.

aSurveiller.texte: The City has until October 31, 2027 to sell a first parcel of land on the site.
The federal grant requires that the infrastructure be completed by 2031.
The temporary leases end on April 30, 2027 (MultiCaf), March 31, 2028 (Polliflora) and April 30, 2028 (transition nursery).

parcs.description: Development and renovation of parks, including the Grand parc de l'Ouest.
parcs.enBref: This year, the City is funding the design and redevelopment work for parks in several boroughs, from parc Le Prévost to parc Baldwin. It is also awarding maintenance and work contracts in the Grand parc de l'Ouest, and submitting the candidacy of the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector for an international night sky designation. Several decisions adjust contracts already underway on park worksites.

etapes.texte: The City is awarding the winning team of an architecture competition the design of the bibliothèque Caroline-Dawson and the redevelopment of parc Le Prévost, for a total expense of $10,559,257.81, taxes included. It is also paying $174,471.56, net of taxes, to the arrondissement de Verdun for soil and environmental studies at parc Monseigneur-J.-A.-Richard, built on a former dump.

The City is adding $162,897.98 to the contract for the repair of the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville, having a culvert under that same road rebuilt, and awarding contracts for snow clearing of service roads and for cutting down ash trees and dying trees. It is submitting the candidacy of the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector for the Urban Night Sky Place designation and registering the Anse-à-l'Orme sector, together with the parc-nature des Sources, in the registry of protected natural areas.

Several decisions add money to, or shift budgets within, worksites already underway: supervision of work at parc du Bassin-à-Bois, parc des Hirondelles, parc du Sault-au-Récollet, parc Villeray, parc Percy-Walters and the museum design of parc des Sœurs de Sainte-Anne.

City council is removing a former 810.2 m² street portion from the public domain as a street in order to add it to parc Campbell Ouest. It is doing the same with a 75.2 m² strip of laneway that crosses parc Le Prévost.

aSurveiller.texte: End of work at parc Denise-Morelle in November 2026, according to the file of the arrondissement du Plateau-Mont-Royal.
Snow clearing of the Grand parc de l'Ouest from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
Housekeeping of nine buildings in the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2030, with a possible extension to October 31, 2031.
For the Cap-Saint-Jacques candidacy: lighting plan submitted in February 2027, DarkSky response expected in April 2027, site compliance work in April 2032.
Final acceptance of work at parc du Bassin-à-Bois expected in June 2027.
End of work at parc J.O.R.-Leduc in June 2028; tree cutting in the Grand parc de l'Ouest until early summer 2028; installation of the artwork at parc des Eaux-Cachées in 2028.

pietonnisation.description: Pedestrian streets, public squares and commercial activity ordinances.
pietonnisation.enBref: This year, the City is organizing the 2026 season of pedestrian streets and public squares: it adopts the funding rules, pays money to boroughs and business development corporations, then closes street sections to cars and regulates sales, noise and traffic on these streets. It also settles a dispute related to the development of a public square, changes the status of a piece of land, and gives a name to a square.

etapes.titre: Funding rules and settlement of a dispute
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie adopts a by-law that allows it to subsidize its business development corporations to pedestrianize streets, up to $425 per linear metre of pedestrianized street. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie settles out of court for $41,686.46 a lawsuit related to the construction work on a public square at the corner of rues Beaubien Est and Boyer.

The boroughs close street sections to cars and authorize terraces, the sale of food and drinks, music and ground painting: Ville-Marie for thirteen streets, Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce for the Placette CDN and the avenues Royal and Madison, Outremont for avenue Bernard, Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve for rue Ontario Est, Le Plateau-Mont-Royal for the avenues du Mont-Royal and Duluth.

The executive committee grants $40,000 to animate the Notre-Dame Ouest pedestrian street from July 10 to 19, 2026 during the FIFA World Cup. Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce closes avenue de Monkland for a commercial promotion from August 20 to 23, 2026, and Ville-Marie authorizes a musical sound ambiance on the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles.

etapes.titre: Public squares and end of season
etapes.texte: City council names the public square at the corner of rue Charleroi and avenue L'Archevêque, in Montréal-Nord, "place Chez-Marguerite," and changes a 899-square-metre piece of land from street status to local park status near the Langelier metro station. Le Plateau-Mont-Royal revises the reopening schedule for avenue du Mont-Royal in three sections.

aSurveiller.texte: Avenue du Mont-Royal reopens to traffic between rue Saint-Denis and rue Resther on September 30, 2026, and between rue Saint-Laurent and rue Saint-Denis on October 15, 2026.
Traffic resumes on the chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges ramp on November 1, 2026, after dismantling on November 1 and 2.
The ordinance on the sound ambiance of the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles runs until September 2, 2027.
The on-demand transportation contract on avenue du Mont-Royal covers the period until December 31, 2027; the 2027 edition will take place only if the pedestrianization project is renewed.
Support for the pedestrianization of avenue Lacombe continues until December 31, 2028: $22,500 in 2027 and $20,000 in 2028.

plan-urbanisme.description: The PUM and the concordance by-laws each borough adopts to comply with it.

etapes.titre: Requests for extension to the ministry
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville is requesting twelve more months, until June 16, 2027, to adopt its concordance by-laws. L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is requesting six additional months, after a first extension obtained in July 2025.

Following the public consultation of March 25, 2026, Ville-Marie is revising its rules on urban planning, special projects, demolition, certificates and cadastral operations. The by-law allows a maximum height of 103 m on the block of the former terrasse Peel and permits public transit stations in category E.1 sectors.

The borough is changing heights, uses and the building footprint ratio in the sector bordered by avenues Papineau, Émile-Journault and André-Grasset and rue Legendre Est, and is increasing allowed heights on stretches of rue Lajeunesse. It is also amending its by-law on the demolition of buildings, following a public meeting held on June 23, 2026.

aSurveiller.texte: Saint-Laurent's public consultation on its three draft by-laws, on October 20, 2026 at 7 p.m.
Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce: public consultation on October 21, 2026 and adoption on November 2, 2026; the extension granted by the minister runs until December 16, 2026.
Saint-Léonard must adopt all its concordance by-laws by June 16, 2027, the date set by the Minister of Municipal Affairs.
Ahuntsic-Cartierville is requesting an extension until June 16, 2027.
Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension has until June 17, 2027 to update its by-laws; its zoning by-law must be replaced in 2027.
L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève plans to present its project to elected officials starting mid-June 2026 and hold a public consultation in September or October 2026.

securite-publique.description: The City of Montréal's police department: contracts, neighbourhood police stations, council motions.

transport-collectif.description: What the City decides about the network: land sold to the STM, areas around stations, agreements.
transport-collectif.enBref: This year, the City approves the budget and loans of the Société de transport de Montréal (STM), and sells, leases or lends it land for its stations, ventilation shafts and staff. It also oversees metro worksites and bus stops on its territory, and entrusts the STM with municipal work related to the extension of the blue line. Borough councils and city council adopt motions on the development of the network.

etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville establishes and removes bus waiting areas as part of the network overhaul, and Saint-Laurent offers to take charge of building sidewalks for the new stops. Ville-Marie authorizes the STM to drill and redo the vault of the green line tunnel 24 hours a day from June 10 to July 31, 2026; the City signs an agreement to build a pavilion attached to the Wiseman ventilation shaft in Outremont, adds a contingency budget to the Berri-UQAM station worksite, and does not oppose the reconstruction of a bridge-tunnel above the REM.

The City entrusts the STM with carrying out its own work at the future Pie-IX and Viau stations, on rue Jean-Talon Est, and authorizes an expenditure of $3,808,451.29, taxes included. It then concludes 72-month framework agreements with Artelia Canada inc. and Stantec Experts-conseils ltée for the design, technical assistance and impact management of the blue line corridor redevelopment.

The agglomeration approves STM loans and amends its capital works program: analysis of the replacement of MR-73 cars, extension of their service life, bus priority measures, Réno-Infrastructures phase 4, surface building repairs, and technological and security risk management.

City council asks Québec to study the conditions for keeping the tunnel boring machine used for the blue line in Montréal. Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles and LaSalle call for structuring public transit projects in the East and in the Grand Sud-Ouest, while Anjou asks the STM to stop the study of a reserved lane on rue Beaubien and avenue du Val-d'Anjou.

aSurveiller.texte: Approval from the ministère des Affaires municipales expected in November 2026 for loans related to the MR-73 cars and surface building repairs.
Work on the Rielle ventilation shaft, in Verdun, is to continue until December 2027.
Rue Wilderton will be closed for a maximum of two weeks during the 2027 summer vacation period, for the reconstruction of the bridge-tunnel; the work is expected to continue until March 2028.
The opening of the five new blue line stations is expected in 2031.

velo.titre: Bike: REV, bike paths and BIXI
velo.description: The Réseau express vélo, bike paths and bike lanes, and the self-service bike system.
velo.enBref: This year, the City and the boroughs are building and repairing bike lanes, managing car traffic around them, and buying equipment for the BIXI system. Work affects the REV Lajeunesse, rue Saint-Jacques, avenue Christophe-Colomb and corridors in Ville-Marie and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve. The City is also settling its rents with Hydro-Québec for land used as bike paths and is asking Québec for financial help for four new projects.

etapes.texte: Outremont authorizes a $100,000 expense, taxes included, for de-icing salt and abrasives spread notably on bike paths. Ahuntsic-Cartierville is renting a mini sweeper with operator for spring cleaning of paths less than 1.8 metres wide.

Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie imposes mandatory manoeuvres on drivers on avenue Christophe-Colomb and formalizes the bike lanes between rue des Carrières and rue de Bellechasse. Outremont tables a draft by-law to convert a shared lane on avenue Lajoie into a one-way bike path, and Ville-Marie makes rue Saint-Jacques one-way eastbound between Peel and Robert-Bourassa for a section of the REV.

The City awards PBSC Solutions Urbaines inc. a sole-source contract of $4,815,802.61, taxes included, for bikes, stations and docking points compatible with BIXI, then a contract of $394,851.17, taxes included, to Laser AMP for the steel bases of the stations. Le Plateau-Mont-Royal and Sud-Ouest each include the installation of a BIXI station in street and laneway projects.

City council approves an agreement of $125,167.62, taxes included, for unpaid rent from 2014 to 2025 on Hydro-Québec land used for bike paths, parks and gardens. It then approves a 10-year lease, starting January 1, 2026, for a strip of about 366 square metres used as a bike path in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles.

etapes.titre: Requests for financial help from Québec
etapes.texte: The City authorizes the filing of four financial assistance requests to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable to build bike lanes and sidewalks on rue de Champlain, rue Saint-Jacques, rue Guy and rue Laurier. It commits to paying at least half of the eligible expenses.

aSurveiller.texte: The new traffic directions and lane assignments on rue Saint-Jacques, linked to the REV, take effect on November 6, 2026.
The lease for the bike path leased from Hydro-Québec in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles runs until December 31, 2035.
